```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(BiocStyle)
```


# Introduction


`r Biocpkg("ZarrArray")` is an infrastructure package that leverages
the `r Biocpkg("Rarr")` package to bring Zarr datasets in R as DelayedArray
objects.

The package implements two main classes:

- The ZarrArray class: ZarrArray objects are array-like objects that
  represent a conventional (i.e. _dense_) Zarr datasets in R.

- The ZarrSparseMatrix class: ZarrSparseMatrix objects are matrix-like
  objects that represent _sparse_ Zarr datasets in R.

Both classes extend the DelayedArray class from the `r Biocpkg("DelayedArray")`
package. This means that ZarrArray and ZarrSparseMatrix objects allow easy
and intuitive R-style array- and matrix-like manipulation of on-disk Zarr
datasets.


# Install and load the package


Like any other Bioconductor package, `r Biocpkg("ZarrArray")` should
_always_ be installed with `BiocManager::install()`:
```{r install, eval=FALSE}
if (!require("BiocManager", quietly=TRUE))
    install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install("ZarrArray")
```

Load the package:
```{r load, message=FALSE}
library(ZarrArray)
```


# ZarrArray objects

The ZarrArray class is a DelayedArray extension for representing and
operating on a conventional (i.e. _dense_) Zarr dataset.
Please check its man page (with `?ZarrArray`) for more information.

## Construction

To construct a ZarrArray object, simply call the `ZarrArray()` constructor
function on the path to a Zarr dataset:
```{r ZarrArray_construction}
zarr_path <- system.file(package="Rarr", "extdata",
                         "zarr_examples", "column-first", "int32.zarr")
A <- ZarrArray(zarr_path)
A
```

## Array and matrix operations

Note that ZarrArray objects are DelayedArray derivatives, and,
therefore, support all operations (delayed or block-processed)
supported by DelayedArray objects:
```{r check_ZarrArray_class}
class(A)

is(A, "DelayedArray")
```

This allows ZarrArray objects to "look and feel" like ordinary arrays or
matrices in R, by mimicking their behavior. In particular, ZarrArray objects
suppport most of the "standard array API" defined in base R like `dim()`,
`length()`, `dimnames()`, `[`, `aperm()`, `max()`, `sum()`, arithmetic and
comparison operations, math functions, etc...
```{r ZarrArray_basic_ops}
dim(A)
length(A)
A[1:5, , 1]
aperm(A)
max(A)
sum(A)
A - 0.5
A^3
A == 0L
sqrt(A)
```

In the 2D case, they also support the "standard matrix API" defined
in base R like `nrow()`, `ncol()`, `rownames()`, `colnames()`, `t()`,
`rbind()`, `cbind()`, `rowSums()`, `colSums()`, `%*%`, etc..., as well
as some row/column summarization operations from the `r CRANpkg("matrixStats")`
package like `rowMaxs()`, `colVars()`, etc...

## Other operations

Other operations are supported that are specific to DelayedArray objects
and their derivatives:
```{r ZarrArray_other_ops}
path(A)
type(A)
chunkdim(A)
a <- as.array(A)
```

See `?ZarrArray` for more information and examples.

## Write an array-like object to disk in Zarr format

The `writeZarrArray()` function can be used to write an array-like
object to disk in Zarr format.

For example we can write back A to disk but with a different physical
chunk geometry:
```{r writeZarrArray_1}
path1 <- tempfile(fileext=".zarr")
writeZarrArray(A, path1, chunkdim=c(3, 5, 2))
```
Or, we can transform A and then write it back to disk:
```{r writeZarrArray_2}
path2 <- tempfile(fileext=".zarr")
A2 <- sqrt(t(A[ , , 1]) + 1)  # all these operations are delayed

## This will realize the delayed operations carried by 'A2' block by block:
writeZarrArray(A2, path2)
```

Note that `writeZarrArray()` leverages lower-level functionality implemented
in the `r Biocpkg("Rarr")` package like `Rarr::create_empty_zarr_array()`
and `Rarr::update_zarr_array()`. See `?writeZarrArray` for more information.


# ZarrSparseMatrix objects

The ZarrSparseMatrix class is a DelayedMatrix extension for representing and
operating on a sparse matrix stored on disk in "Zarr sparse" format.

For the examples in this section, we're going to use a zipped AnnData-style
file from the `r Biocpkg("anndataR")` package that contains a collection of
Zarr-based sparse matrices.

```{r install_and_load_anndataR, message=FALSE}
if (!require("anndataR", quietly=TRUE))
    BiocManager::install("anndataR")

library(anndataR)
anndataR_extdata <- system.file(package="anndataR", "extdata")
list.files(anndataR_extdata)  # 3 files
```

Please refer to the Examples section of the ZarrSparseMatrix man page (with
`?ZarrSparseMatrix`) for a quick overview of what's in these files.

The file that we're interested in is `example_v3.zarr.zip`, but we need
to unzip it first:
```{r unzip_example_v3.zarr.zip}
zad_basename <- "example_v3.zarr"  # zad: Zarr-based AnnData
zad_zip <- paste0(zad_basename, ".zip")
zad_zip_path <- file.path(anndataR_extdata, zad_zip)
exdir <- tempdir()
unzip(zad_zip_path, exdir=exdir)
zad_store <- file.path(exdir, zad_basename)
```

## Construction

To construct a ZarrSparseMatrix object, simply call the `ZarrSparseMatrix()`
constructor function specifying the path to the Zarr store and group where
the sparse matrix is located:
```{r ZarrSparseMatrix_construction}
ZSM <- ZarrSparseMatrix(zad_store, "/X")
ZSM
```

## Matrix operations

Like ZarrArray objects, ZarrSparseMatrix objects are also DelayedArray
derivatives, and, therefore, also support all operations (delayed or
block-processed) supported by DelayedArray objects:
```{r check_ZarrSparseMatrix_class}
class(ZSM)

is(ZSM, "DelayedMatrix")

## The DelayedMatrix class extends the DelayedArray class:
is(ZSM, "DelayedArray")
```

ZarrSparseMatrix objects to "look and feel" like ordinary matrices in R:
```{r ZarrSparseMatrix_basic_ops}
dim(ZSM)
length(ZSM)

ZSM[1:5, 1:6]
ZSM[1:5 , 50]
t(ZSM)

max(ZSM)
sum(ZSM)

ZSM - 0.5
ZSM^3
ZSM == 0L
sqrt(ZSM)

head(rowSums(ZSM))
head(rowMaxs(ZSM))
head(colVars(ZSM))
```

## Other operations

Other operations are supported that are specific to DelayedArray objects
and their derivatives:
```{r ZarrSparseMatrix_other_ops}
path(ZSM)
group(ZSM)

type(ZSM)
chunkdim(ZSM)
is_sparse(ZSM)
zsm <- as.matrix(ZSM)
```

See `?ZarrSparseMatrix` for more information and examples.

## Write a matrix-like object as a Zarr-based sparse matrix

The `writeZarrSparseMatrix()` function can be used to write a matrix-like
object (typically sparse) to disk in "Zarr sparse" format:
```{r writeZarrSparseMatrix_1}
m0 <- matrix(0L, nrow=25, ncol=12,
             dimnames=list(letters[1:25], LETTERS[1:12]))
m0[cbind(2:24, c(12:1, 2:12))] <- 100L + sample(55L, 23, replace=TRUE)

zarr_store <- tempfile(fileext=".zarr")
ZSM0 <- writeZarrSparseMatrix(m0, zarr_store, group="/X0")
ZSM0
```

`path()` and `group()`:
```{r path_and_group_of_ZarrSparseMatrix}
path(ZSM0)
group(ZSM0)
```

The object passed to `writeZarrSparseMatrix()` can be a matrix-like object of
any sort. For example, it can be a dgCMatrix object from the `r Biocpkg("Matrix")`
package:
```{r writeZarrSparseMatrix_2}
library(Matrix)
dgc <- as(m0, "dgCMatrix")
ZSM1 <- writeZarrSparseMatrix(dgc, zarr_store, group="/X1")
ZSM1

path(ZSM1)
group(ZSM1)
```

or it can be a DelayedMatrix object:
```{r writeZarrSparseMatrix_3}
SM2 <- log(ZSM1[ , 7:12] + 1)  # all these operations are delayed
is_sparse(SM2)

## This will realize the delayed operations carried by 'SM2' block by block:
ZSM2 <- writeZarrSparseMatrix(SM2, zarr_store, group="/X2")
ZSM2

path(ZSM2)
group(ZSM2)
```

Etc...

Note that `writeZarrSparseMatrix()` leverages lower-level functionality
implemented in the `r Biocpkg("Rarr")` package like
`Rarr::write_zarr_group()`, `Rarr::create_empty_zarr_array()`,
and `Rarr::update_zarr_array()`. See `?writeZarrSparseMatrix` for more
information.
